g.text: Ask to find their pensions
From the overview of their pots, the
saver asks to find their pensions.
Before anything happens they are
told what will: every UK pension
provider is searched, through the
pension-finding service; they prove
who they are to the service, not to
Pot Tracker; and providers answer
over days, not seconds.
Search again within the year
The saver searched before, and the
consent they gave then has not
ended. They are told when they
agreed and until when, and search
again without proving who they are
or agreeing again.
Prove who they are
The saver proves who they are to the
pension-finding service, in its own
window: its identity check is not
this UI's. Pot Tracker waits, saying
what the service will ask for and
that it never sees it, and carries
on when the service says whether it
succeeded.
02a · end
Cannot prove who they are
The service could not confirm who
the saver is. Pot Tracker sees only
that, not why, so it says what
commonly causes it and how to try
again. No search starts.
End: the search has not started.
Agree to the search
The saver agrees to two things,
separately: that the service may
search for their pensions, and that
Pot Tracker may receive what it
finds. They are told the agreement
lasts a year, and until when. The
search starts only once both are
agreed.
03a · end
Decline the search
The saver does not agree. No search
is made and nothing is shared, and
they are told so.
End: no search was made and nothing
was shared.
See the search start
The search starts, and the saver is
told it has, and when. It is not a
wait on a spinner: they are told
that providers answer over days,
that they need not stay, and that
they will be told what is found.
See pensions arrive
As each provider answers, its
pension is added to the saver's
pots, newest first: the provider,
the employer it came from, that it
is a pot of money, and its value
with its date. Each is marked as
found by the search, and the count
goes up.
Receive a possible match
A provider can only say it may hold
a pension for the saver. It is
listed as a possible match, not a
pot, with the provider's reason for
not being sure, for the saver to
claim when they choose. The search
carries on.
The walkthrough
analysis/ui/walkthroughs/claim-a-pos
sible-match (not written yet)
Receive a pension with no
value yet
A provider has found the pension but
cannot give its value yet. It is
added as a pot with no value, saying
when one is expected.
Find a pension already added
The search finds the SIPP the saver
had already added by hand as a
portfolio. It is not added twice:
the pot they added is marked as
found by the search too.
06 · end
Be told the search has
finished
Every provider has answered. The
saver is told the search has
finished and how many pensions it
found, and back on the overview the
pots it found are among their pots,
each marked so.
End: every pension found is one of
the saver's pots.
06a · end
Find no pensions
Every provider answered with
nothing. The saver is told no
pension was found, and offered
adding an ISA or investment account
instead.
End: no pension was found, and
adding a portfolio is offered.
06b · end
Be told what was found while
away
The saver signed out while the
search ran. Answers kept arriving,
and when they next sign in the
overview tells them how many
pensions were found since they were
last there, and that the search is
still running.
End: the saver knows what the search
found while they were away.
